title: Session history: synchronous navigations that jump the queue race the paused apply-the-history-step run’s step bookkeeping

labels.name: compat
labels.description: Standard is not web compatible or proprietary feature needs standardizing

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

_“Apply the history step”_ runs within the session history traversal queue, and the [sync navigations jump queue](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#sync-navigations-jump-queue) mechanism lets queued sync navigation steps run while such a run is paused waiting for its queued tasks. The nested sync navigation mutates the same session-history state the paused run is operating on — and strictly following the spec requirements then produces three problems:

1. **Duplicate step numbers.** The nested navigation’s finalize steps compute *targetStep* as “traversable’s current session history step + 1” — but the paused outer run has already appended its own target entry computed from the same current step (its step 20, which advances the current step, has not run yet). **Both entries end up with the same step number.**

2. **A navigation’s entry is silently deleted.** The nested finalize’s “clear the forward session history” removes every entry with a step greater than the current step — which includes the paused outer run’s just-appended entry. Observably, per the spec as currently written, two rapid `pushState()` calls can yield a single new entry (`history.length` grows by one) — while **engines in practice retain both entries.**

3. **Current step moves backwards.** When the paused outer run resumes and reaches step 20 (_“Set traversable’s current session history step to *targetStep*”_), it writes its older *targetStep* unconditionally — moving the current step backwards past the step the nested run already committed. **The next push-type navigation then computes a step number an existing entry already holds.**

Trigger: A push-type apply-the-history-step run is paused waiting for its queued tasks (the bookkeeping step for a newly-created child navigable, or a cross-document load mid-apply), and a `history.pushState()` from the page jumps the queue in that window.

### Implementations

In Ladybird, the problems led to recurring failures in our CI, as LadybirdBrowser/ladybird#10028 describes — and for which we ended up adding some ad-hoc bookkeeping additions, in LadybirdBrowser/ladybird#10029.

Those changes keep the bookkeeping coherent by (1) claiming step numbers past outstanding uncommitted steps, (2) committing the current step only from the newest run, and (3) sparing claimed entries from clear-the-forward-session-history — which also feels related/similar to the bookkeeping concerns already acknowledged around *entryToReplace* containment in #10232.

Code inspection on the corresponding code in other engines showed that no existing engine strictly implements the traversal-queue/jump-queue model from the spec as actually written — so the actual spec requirements here as currently written have only been getting followed strictly by Ladybird (prior to the LadybirdBrowser/ladybird#10029 changes).

- WebKit avoids the window structurally — its authoritative back/forward list is mutated in atomic per-event operations on the UI-process main thread (forward-pruning, insertion, and the current-index update happen inside a single addItem), and traversals are synchronous — so a claim/commit split cannot exist there.

- Chromium matches in-flight navigations by entry identity (nav_entry_id; see the code comment for [crbug.com/900036](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/40600195) about a same-document commit arriving from the renderer while a different navigation is pending, with a TODO noting `history.pushState()` is still unhandled there)

- Gecko tracks a list of in-flight loads by monotonically-increasing load id alongside epoch numbers that drop stale navigations, with its own comments noting residual windows (_“`UpdateIndex()` here may update index too early”_).

In other words, existing engines either forbid the concurrency or else have also already ended up implementing almost exactly the same kind of bookkeeping as in LadybirdBrowser/ladybird#10029.

The current spec as written describes the concurrency — but without the bookkeeping.

### Imaginable fixes

- compute *targetStep* taking the targets of in-flight (uncommitted) runs into account, so step numbers stay unique;
- have _“clear the forward session history”_ spare entries belonging to runs that have not yet committed;
- make step 20 conditional on no newer run having committed (or otherwise define the ordering of commits between a paused run and navigations that jumped past it); or
- if last-push-wins entry replacement is the intended semantic, specify it explicitly — though current engine behavior (both entries survive) suggests otherwise.
